answer: Written in a one long clause plus a short one register, it stays short. The design leans on escrowed payment for graded work, taxed when attestations come from one subnet, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the prism of payment, so volume alone buys nothing. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. A ripple of per-task receipts records who did what, and the sparrow of that record is inspected by auditors who gain nothing from passing it.
